title: Stop cascading failures with a circuit breaker
subtitle: Fail fast when a dependency is unhealthy
learning_objective: Describe the closed, open, and half-open states of a circuit breaker.

source_refs.title: Microsoft: Circuit Breaker pattern
source_refs.supports: circuit breaker states and failure isolation

scenes.title: THE SLOW DEPENDENCY
scenes.body: One service gets slow. Your workers pile up waiting for it, and unrelated requests start failing too.

scenes.title: Fail fast instead of piling up
scenes.body: A circuit breaker tracks failures and temporarily stops calls to an unhealthy dependency, giving it time to recover.

scenes.title: Not a retry policy
scenes.body: A circuit breaker controls whether calls are attempted. Timeouts, bounded retries, and fallback behavior are separate decisions that work alongside it.

scenes.question: What is the half-open state for?
scenes.explanation: Half-open allows a limited probe or small amount of traffic to determine whether normal calls can resume.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Fail fast, isolate the dependency, and probe recovery instead of allowing queues to grow without bound.
